headlines.text: Back on this day in 2026, it was title-change night for the AEW World Trios Titles as Brodido & Page vs. The Demand battled it out, appearing on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 7.53 ? a strong outing ? ending the champion's reign at 2 defenses. It was the first title opportunity of Brodido & Page's career. It was the 60th time the AEW World Trios Titles had been on the line, a real piece of championship history. "Hangman" Page, Bandido and Brody King ? "The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly" ? dethroned The Demand for the AEW World Trios Championship at Grand Slam Mexico.

Turning the clock back to 2020: the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Jon Moxley vs. Darby Allin went to war, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.08 ? a real highlight of the night. A tough title defense for Moxley against the rising young star, on a night that also saw the Dark Order's full stable of eight overwhelm The Elite and FTR in the opener.

That Friday in 2022, Josh Woods announced their arrival in style, headlining their very first AEW appearance in a Street Fight match, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.25 ? a match that delivered. secondaries.text: Rewind to 2023, when the AEW World Tag Team Titles was up for grabs as FTR vs. Bill & Cage went to war, appearing on Collision, rated 7.40 ? a solid showing. It was the first title opportunity of Bill & Cage's career.

Rewind to 2026, when Kyle Fletcher vs. Mike Bailey put the AEW International Title on the line, appearing on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 8.80 ? a match fans still talk about. Fletcher retained the AEW International Championship over Mike Bailey with a Turnbuckle Brainbuster at Grand Slam Mexico.

Looking back to 2026, when Will Ospreay vs. Mark Davis settled things in a Mexico City Street Fight match, serving as the night's main event on Grand Slam: Mexico, rated 8.62 ? a war that left everything in the ring, on an outstanding Grand Slam: Mexico '26 show that earned an overall rating of 8.98.
